10.1: Hear again My supreme word, which I declare to you who are delighted, for your welfare.
10.2: Neither the gods nor the great sages know My origin, for I am the source of them all.
10.3: One who knows Me as unborn, beginningless and the great Lord of the worlds is undeluded and freed from all sins.
10.4: Intelligence, knowledge, non-delusion, patience, truth, self-control, calmness, pleasure, pain, birth, death, fear and fearlessness —
10.5: — non-injury, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and disgrace: these varied states of beings arise from Me alone.
10.6: The seven great sages and the four ancients and the Manus were born of My mind; from them came these creatures.
10.7: One who truly knows this glory and power of Mine is united with unshakable yoga — of this there is no doubt.
10.8: I am the origin of all; everything proceeds from Me — knowing this, the wise worship Me with loving conviction.
10.9: With minds fixed on Me, lives surrendered to Me, enlightening one another and speaking of Me, they are content and delighted.
10.10: To those ever steadfast and worshipping with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to Me.
10.11: Out of compassion, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
10.12: Arjuna responds: you are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier, eternal, divine, the primal God.
10.13: All the sages have said this of you, and now you yourself tell me so.
10.14: I hold all you say to be true; neither gods nor demons know your manifestation.
10.15: You alone know yourself by yourself, O supreme Person, source of beings, Lord of all, God of gods.
10.16: Please describe in full your divine glories, by which you pervade and abide in these worlds.
10.17: How may I know you by constant meditation, and in what aspects should I think of you?
10.18: Tell me again in detail of your power and glory, for I am never satisfied hearing your nectar-like words.
10.19: Krishna agrees: I shall tell you the chief of My divine glories, for there is no end to My extent.
10.20: I am the Self seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all.
10.21: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights the radiant sun; among the Maruts Marichi; among stars the moon.
10.22: Among Vedas the Sama; among gods Indra; among senses the mind; and in beings I am consciousness.
10.23: Among Rudras I am Shankara; among treasure-keepers Kubera; among Vasus fire; among mountains Meru.
10.24: Among priests I am Brihaspati; among generals Skanda; among waters the ocean.
10.25: Among great sages Bhrigu; among words the single syllable Om; among sacrifices the sacrifice of silent repetition; among immovables the Himalaya.
10.26: Among trees the ashvattha; among divine sages Narada; among Gandharvas Chitraratha; among perfected ones Kapila.
10.27: Among horses Uchchaihshravas born of nectar; among elephants Airavata; among men the king.
10.28: Among weapons the thunderbolt; among cows Kamadhenu; I am the progenitor Kandarpa; among serpents Vasuki.
10.29: Among Nagas Ananta; among water-beings Varuna; among ancestors Aryama; among controllers Yama.
10.30: Among demons Prahlada; among reckoners Time; among beasts the lion; among birds Garuda.
10.31: Among purifiers the wind; among warriors Rama; among fishes the shark; among rivers the Ganga.
10.32: I am the beginning, middle and end of creation; among sciences the science of the Self; among debaters the logic of truth.
10.33: Among letters the letter A; among compounds the dual; I am imperishable time and the dispenser facing everywhere.
10.34: I am all-devouring death and the origin of things to be; among feminine qualities fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and patience.
10.35: Among hymns the Brihat-saman; among metres Gayatri; among months Margashirsha; among seasons spring.
10.36: I am the gambling of the deceitful, the splendour of the splendid, victory, effort, and the goodness of the good.
10.37: Among the Vrishnis I am Krishna; among Pandavas Arjuna; among sages Vyasa; among poets Ushana.
10.38: I am the sceptre of rulers, the statecraft of the victory-seeking, the silence of secrets, and the knowledge of the knowing.
10.39: Whatever is the seed of all beings, that too am I; nothing moving or unmoving can exist without Me.
10.40: There is no end to My divine glories; what I have declared is only a fraction, by way of illustration.
10.41: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful, know it to spring from a fragment of My splendour.
10.42: But what use is all this detail to you? I stand supporting this whole universe with a single fragment of Myself.
